subject: ADR-200: the claim moves to the act -- a task says what the page said, and the kit's second message convention
body: ADR-199 gave every act `said` and closed by saying it had not made the six steps polling boxes.toast correct, only unnecessary. This is that slice, and the first thing it found is that THE GRAMMAR COULD NOT STATE THE CLAIM AT ALL. `said` is a LIST OF STRINGS and the claim a task wants about it is almost never exact equality -- a refusal reads 'model logistic needs 4 parameters' and the task is about the first half -- while `contains` on a list is exact membership of ONE ELEMENT, deliberately, because a table row is written as a list of cells and widening it would quietly loosen every list claim in the kit. So `any-contains` and `none-contains`: some element holds this text, and its mirror. THE MIRROR IS NOT SYMMETRY FOR ITS OWN SAKE -- absence is a claim, and a task that cannot state it states a guess instead, ADR-132's lesson one container deeper; the claim this slice could not have written before is on the experiment guide's SECOND model, that having refused logistic with two parameters the page does not repeat the refusal when four arrive. Three edges, each with a check and a mutant: a path that is not a list is FALSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because answering either way about a string would let a task claim about boxes.toast through the very grammar built to get it off boxes.toast; a missing path does not prove silence, the rule `excludes` already carries; and `contains` is UNCHANGED, a second claim rather than a loosening of the old one. SIX STEPS MOVED, FOUR DISAPPEARED: each read-report of the toast box -- a whole report taken inside a 1.7-second window against a box holding whatever the LAST message was -- is now a claim on the act that raised it, the protocol library's copy also claiming produced==1 and the two refusals produced==0; four of those read-reports existed ONLY for the race and are gone, and a check scans every task file rather than trusting that list. Every claim that moved was confirmed against the real runner before it was written down, which is how the protocol library's two-way `in` turned out to be hedging about a clipboard fallback that never fires under the door. AND THE KIT HAD TWO MESSAGE CONVENTIONS. A probe that presses every control on every page and watches for text appearing OUTSIDE a live region found the rest of ADR-199's blind spot: two pages answer in a PERSISTENT STATUS LINE -- a dedicated msg(text, bad) that writes a sentence into a paragraph and colours it red when the news is bad -- greenhouse #runMsg and #srcMsg, and tree-visualizer #msg, a page this kit's .toast convention had never touched. The greenhouse's 'Load a source first -- there is nothing to save.' is the ENTIRE outcome of that press, with nothing else on screen to say the run was not saved, and it reached neither a screen reader nor the door. All three declare role=status aria-live=polite now. PINNED RATHER THAN PATTERN-MATCHED: whether an element is a message or a caption is a judgement -- the greenhouse's #logNote ('337 readings loaded') is a caption on what a render just drew -- so the list states the judgement instead of a regex pretending to make it. verify_tasks 371 -> 380, verify_report 237 -> 242, mutate_tasks 80 -> 87, mutate_report 141 -> 145, all killed.
